```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse  = TRUE,
  comment   = "#>",
  fig.width  = 8,
  fig.height = 5,
  message   = FALSE,
  warning   = FALSE,
  eval      = !identical(Sys.getenv("CI"), "true")
)
```

Many public health datasets in India report indicators as raw counts.
Comparing raw counts across geographies is misleading, a larger state
will always report more events simply due to population size. The
standard solution is to normalize the raw counts, for instance
calculating malaria incidence (per 100,000) in place of just raw malaria
case/test/deaths counts.

`{censusindia}` provides **annual district- and state-level population
projections from 2012 to 2031**, modeled from the 2011 Census by the
Registrar General of India (RGI).

This vignette demonstrates the workflow using malaria death data from
the Health Management Information System (HMIS), accessed via
`{hmisindia}`. The two packages are designed to work together:
`hmisindia` provides the numerator, `censusindia` provides the
denominator.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Setup

```{r packages}
library(censusindia)   # population projections 
library(hmisindia)     # HMIS data
library(arrow)         # read parquet files 
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)     # side-by-side plots

#district_path <- "path/to/hmis_long_district.parquet"
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What {censusindia} Provides

```{r show-projections}
# State-level projections: annual, 2011-2031
glimpse(population_projections_state)

# District-level projections with LGD codes
glimpse(population_projections_district_lgd)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Data Preparation

### State-level malaria deaths (HMIS)

```{r state-fetch}
falciparum_deaths <- get_disease_deaths("Malaria (Pf)",
                                        sector   = "Total",
                                        category = "Total")

vivax_deaths      <- get_disease_deaths("Malaria (Pv)",
                                        sector   = "Total",
                                        category = "Total")

malaria_deaths_raw <- bind_rows(
  falciparum_deaths |> mutate(species = "Falciparum"),
  vivax_deaths      |> mutate(species = "Vivax")
) |>
  filter(!cal_year %in% c(2024, 2025))  
```

```{r state-aggregate}
malaria_annual <- malaria_deaths_raw |>
  filter(
    state != "All India",
    !state %in% hmis_non_geo_states,                      # removes M/O Defence, Railways
    !grepl("Dadra|Daman", state, ignore.case = TRUE)      # drop merged UT (boundary mismatch)
  ) |>
  group_by(state, cal_year, species) |>
  summarise(deaths = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

### Attach the {censusindia} population denominator

```{r pop-state}
pop_total <- population_projections_state |>
  select(state_name_harmonized, year, population)
```

### Join and compute rate

```{r state-join}
malaria_rate <- malaria_annual |>
  left_join(
    pop_total,
    by = c("state" = "state_name_harmonized", "cal_year" = "year")
  ) |>
  mutate(rate_per_100k = (deaths / population) * 1e5) |>
  filter(!is.na(rate_per_100k), !is.infinite(rate_per_100k), population > 0) |>
  filter(cal_year >= 2017, cal_year <= 2023)
```

### District-level data

```{r district-fetch}
falciparum_dist <- open_dataset(district_path) |>
  filter(canonical_name == "Number of Deaths due to Malaria - Plasmodium Falciparum",
         sector   == "Total",
         category == "Total") |>
  collect() |>
  add_calendar_vars() |>
  filter(
    !state %in% hmis_non_geo_states,
    !grepl("Dadra|Daman", state, ignore.case = TRUE)
  ) |>
  group_by(state, district, cal_year) |>
  summarise(deaths = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

vivax_dist <- open_dataset(district_path) |>
  filter(canonical_name == "Number of Deaths due to Malaria - Plasmodium Vivax",
         sector   == "Total",
         category == "Total") |>
  collect() |>
  add_calendar_vars() |>
  filter(
    !state %in% hmis_non_geo_states,
    !grepl("Dadra|Daman", state, ignore.case = TRUE)
  ) |>
  group_by(state, district, cal_year) |>
  summarise(deaths = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

malaria_dist <- bind_rows(
  falciparum_dist |> mutate(species = "Falciparum"),
  vivax_dist      |> mutate(species = "Vivax")
)
```

```{r district-join}
pop_dist <- population_projections_district_lgd |>
  select(state_name_harmonized, district, year, population)

malaria_dist_rate <- malaria_dist |>
  left_join(
    pop_dist,
    by = c("state"    = "state_name_harmonized",
           "district" = "district",
           "cal_year" = "year")
  ) |>
  mutate(rate_per_100k = (deaths / population) * 1e5) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(rate_per_100k),
    !is.infinite(rate_per_100k),
    population > 0,
    cal_year >= 2017,
    cal_year <= 2023
  )
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Raw Count vs. Normalised Rate

The same 10 states ranked by total raw deaths, shown side by side. Raw
counts (left) and malaria incidence after normalization (right).

```{r bar-plots, fig.width=14, fig.height=5}
# for both bar plots, exclude Telangana (its 2018 outbreak spike disproportionately inflates the mean)

top_states <- malaria_rate |>
  filter(state != "Telangana") |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(total_deaths = sum(deaths)) |>
  slice_max(total_deaths, n = 10) |>
  pull(state)

p1 <- malaria_rate |>
  filter(state %in% top_states) |>
  group_by(state, species) |>
  summarise(deaths = sum(deaths), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(state, deaths), y = deaths, fill = species)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Falciparum" = "steelblue4", "Vivax" = "tan3")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    title    = "Raw Count",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Deaths (absolute count)",
    fill     = "Species",
    caption  = "Data: HMIS via {hmisindia}"
  ) +
  theme_hmis() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        axis.text = element_text(face = "bold"))

p2 <- malaria_rate |>
  filter(state %in% top_states) |>
  group_by(state, species) |>
  summarise(
    deaths     = sum(deaths),
    population = mean(population),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(rate_per_100k = (deaths / population) * 1e5) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(state, rate_per_100k), y = rate_per_100k, fill = species)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Falciparum" = "steelblue", "Vivax" = "tan3")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Normalised Rate (per 100,000)",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Deaths per 100,000 population",
    fill     = "Species",
    caption  = "HMIS & RGI population projections via {censusindia}"
  ) +
  theme_hmis() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        axis.text = element_text(face = "bold"))

p1 + p2 +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Total Malaria Deaths by State (2017–2023)",
    theme    = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"))
  )
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Normalized Death Rate Trend

```{r line-normalised, fig.height=5}
high_burden <- malaria_rate |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(mean_rate = mean(rate_per_100k)) |>
  slice_max(mean_rate, n = 6) |>
  pull(state)

malaria_rate |>
  filter(state %in% high_burden) |>
  group_by(state, cal_year) |>
  summarise(
    rate_per_100k = sum(deaths) / mean(population) * 1e5,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = cal_year, y = rate_per_100k, colour = state)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  facet_wrap(~ state, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title    = "Malaria Death Rate Trend (per 100,000)",
    subtitle = "Top 6 states by HMIS-reported normalised rate  |  Falciparum & Vivax combined",
caption  = "Note: Rankings reflect HMIS facility reporting; states with low health facility utilisation may be underrepresented. \n Data: HMIS & RGI population projections via {censusindia}",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Deaths (per 100,000)",
    colour   = NULL) +
  theme_hmis() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",   # redundant with facet labels
    axis.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## District Choropleth Maps

District-level normalized rates reveal geographic concentration of
malaria burden that state totals obscure.
`censusindia::population_projections_district_lgd` provides the district
denominators; `hmisindia::attach_geometry()` attaches LGD boundaries for
mapping.

> Note: 79% of district-year observations have zero malaria deaths,
> malaria is highly focal, concentrated in tribal belt districts of
> Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and parts of the northeast. Values
> above the 99th percentile are capped to prevent a handful of extreme
> districts from collapsing the colour scale.

```{r map-combined, fig.height=8}
# run once before all maps
state_borders <- censusindia::get_census_boundaries(year = 2011, geography = "state")

plot_district_map <- function(data, title, subtitle = "") {
  data |>
    hmisindia::attach_geometry() |>
    ggplot(aes(fill = rate_plot)) +
    geom_sf(colour = "grey45", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_sf(data = state_borders, fill = NA,
            colour = "royalblue4", linewidth = 0.35) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      option    = "magma",
      direction = -1,
      name      = "Deaths\n(per 100k)",
      labels    = comma_format(accuracy = 1)
    ) +
    labs(
      title    = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      caption  = "Values above 99th percentile capped. Data: HMIS & RGI population projections via {censusindia}"
    ) +
    theme_hmis() +
    theme(
      axis.text       = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks      = element_blank(),
      panel.grid      = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "top"
    ) +
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(barwidth = 14, barheight = 0.65))
}

# combined map
malaria_dist_rate |>
  group_by(state, district) |>
  summarise(
    rate_per_100k = sum(deaths) / mean(population) * 1e5,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(rate_plot = pmin(rate_per_100k, quantile(rate_per_100k, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  plot_district_map(
    title    = "Malaria Death Rate by District (2017–2023) | Falciparum + Vivax combined"
  )

# per-species maps
for(sp in c("Falciparum", "Vivax")) {
  p <- malaria_dist_rate |>
    filter(species == sp) |>
    group_by(state, district) |>
    summarise(
      rate_per_100k = sum(deaths) / mean(population) * 1e5,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(rate_plot = pmin(rate_per_100k, quantile(rate_per_100k, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
    plot_district_map(
      title    = paste("Malaria Death Rate by District -", sp)
    )
  print(p)
}
```
